beats.heading: Hook: a growl and an early hit
beats.narration_text: A wolf growls before it lunges. Hit it during the growl, and the lunge is cancelled. This is my game as it runs today, played by scripted input.

beats.heading: What it is
beats.narration_text: I'm Zhefan Zhang. My final project is The Little Flame Witch, an H-D two-D cave adventure shooter: a little witch fights through one cave with fireballs and defeats a great wolf. It will be a playable Windows build of one vertical slice, title screen to end screen.
beats.script_text: I'm Zhefan Zhang. My final project is The Little Flame Witch, an HD-2D cave adventure shooter: a little witch fights through one cave with fireballs and defeats a great wolf. It will be a playable Windows build of one vertical slice, title screen to end screen.
beats.label: constructed

qc.contrast_reason: Title text over a darkened real capture of the cave; the plate is full-bleed by design, so contrast is measured on the title block.

beats.heading: Why anyone would care
beats.narration_text: Why care? It will put Octopath Traveler's H-D two-D look together with Metal Slug-style side-scrolling, with a mouse-aimed fireball. Octopath is turn-based, Metal Slug fires in fixed directions, Hollow Knight is a large cave with progression; I've played all three. This will be a short action run.

beats.heading: The look
beats.narration_text: The look will come from Godot's own renderer: tilt-shift depth of field, bloom, a cold blue cave where only fire is warm, light shafts through fog, and the fireball as a moving light, each one visual only, with my behaviour pin still passing.

beats.narration_text: Four short, skippable story moments will use portraits. The opening: The fire in my staff is the only warm thing down here. Let's see where this cave goes.

beats.narration_text: Before the boss, the great wolf: Turn back, little flame. This cave is mine. And the witch: Then I'll light my own way.

beats.heading: Who opens it: the first sixty seconds
beats.narration_text: Who opens it? A hiring manager or a lead gameplay programmer; my target role is gameplay programmer. In the first sixty seconds they'll unzip it, double-click the E-X-E, see the controls on the title screen, skip the opening line with one key, and be playing within a minute.

beats.heading: What it proves: the pin and the tests
beats.narration_text: I pinned the behaviour every physics tick before that change; only the two scenarios with a hit during the growl changed. Thirty-eight headless test runs passed in a fresh clone. The slice's frame time will be measured on an R-T-X fifty-sixty Laptop GPU.

beats.heading: In, out, first
beats.narration_text: In: one cave level from title to end screen, with a heal spell, the great-wolf boss, spikes, a boulder, a chest, a campfire, the story moments and a Windows build. Out: multiplayer. First: the core loop in one three-D cave room. It ran if my existing behaviour pin passes there and a windowed capture shows it, labelled with its revision.

beats.heading: The risk, and the pin as its test
beats.narration_text: The risk: moving the two-D game into three-D could break movement, collision and state machines that work today. A two-D gameplay layer in front of a three-D cave, or three-D bodies held to a plane? A one-room spike will decide, judged by my Assignment 7 pin. If it fails, the two-D layer stays and the three-D is backdrop.
beats.script_text: The risk: moving the 2D game into 3D could break movement, collision and state machines that work today. A 2D gameplay layer in front of a 3D cave, or 3D bodies held to a plane? A one-room spike will decide, judged by my Assignment 7 pin. If it fails, the 2D layer stays and the 3D is backdrop.

beats.heading: Exists today, and what will exist
beats.narration_text: Today: the two-D game, its animation, shaders, particles and tests, the Assignment 3 props, and concept portraits not yet in the game. Everything else will exist: the three-D cave and its look, the story in the game, the heal spell, the boss, hazards, the rest point, title and end screens, the Windows build and its test report.
